headline: Sales grow, GAAP profit falls on one-off costs
summary_short: Genuine Parts Company reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $6.54B, up 6.0% y/y, while diluted EPS of $1.65 fell 9.8% y/y as $92.6M of restructuring and separation costs — nearly double last year's — weighed on GAAP profit; adjusted diluted EPS rose to $2.15 from $2.10.
summary_long: Net sales rose 6.0% y/y to $6.54B (3.4% comparable, 1.4% FX, 1.2% acquisitions), with Industrial segment EBITDA margin up 30bp to 13.1% and North America Automotive up 20bp to 8.2%, while International Automotive margin fell 20bp to 9.4% on acquisition dilution. GAAP diluted EPS fell 9.8% y/y to $1.65 as restructuring and separation costs roughly doubled to $92.6M pretax; adjusted diluted EPS rose to $2.15 from $2.10. Cash was $559.1M, long-term debt $3.98B, and total liquidity $2.3B. GPC reaffirmed full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $7.50-8.00 but lowered GAAP EPS guidance to $5.90-6.40 from $6.10-6.60, raising International Automotive sales-growth guidance to 5-8% while trimming North America Automotive to 2.5-4.5%.

drivers.explanation: Comparable sales grew 3.4% plus a 1.4% FX tailwind and 1.2% from acquisitions; Industrial led with 6.1% comparable growth, North America Automotive 2.6%, International Automotive 0.6%.
GAAP EPS fell as restructuring and Global Automotive/Global Industrial separation costs rose to $92.6M pretax from $45.7M a year ago; adjusted EPS, which excludes these, rose to $2.15 from $2.10.

Management reaffirmed full-year adjusted EPS guidance ($7.50-8.00) but lowered GAAP EPS guidance to $5.90-6.40 from $6.10-6.60, raised International Automotive sales-growth guidance to 5-8%, and trimmed North America Automotive to 2.5-4.5%.
